title: Romualdez flood control case can be done in a year --Ombudsman
summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday said that former House speaker Martin Romualdez"s case can be done in one year, especially after one of the co-accused surrendered to authorities.

blocks.text: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday said that former House speaker Martin Romualdez’s case can be done in one year, especially after one of the co-accused surrendered to authorities.

Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. President Felicito Guevarra, a co-accused of both Romualdez and former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co, surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) after the prosecution moved to cancel his passport.
Speaking on a program on DZRH, Remulla said that Guevarra returned around P324 million to the government. The amount was allegedly accumulated from commissions he earned from transactions.

“Money changer yun, yun yun komisyon niya sa transaction. Testifying siya ngayon. Kaya we’re looking at the case now, of the former speaker, parang kung talagang bail hearing ang kanilang habol, ang sinasabi ko, let’s present our evidence in chief already. Tapusin na natin 'to,” Remulla said.

(That was a money change, that was his commission from transactions. He is testifying now. So we’re looking at the case now, of the former speaker. If they really want a bail hearing, I said, let’s present our evidence in chief already. We should finish this.)
“I signed an immunity agreement already. Talagang state witness na yun… Witness for the Ombudsman yan,” he added.
(I have signed an immunity agreement already. He really is a state witness now… a witness for the Ombudsman.)
Remulla is also optimistic that they could finish the case in "record time," adding that he does not want any delaying tactics. Cases that are pursued aggressively could be finished fast.

“Pero within a one year period. Pwedeng tapusin namin yung case namin. Kasi umaabot yan ng 15 years nung nakaraan. Nagyon, kasi we’re ready before we file, ready kami magpresent ng evidence,” Remulla said.
(But within one year. We could finish the case then. Because in the past, it reached 15 years. Now, we’re ready before we file, we are ready to present evidence.)

Romualdez and Co are facing a P7.44 billion plunder case in relation to the flood control scam, which saw lawmakers and officials funneling public funds into bogus infrastructure projects. Both have denied the allegations against them. —VAL, GMA News
